staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this prepared gpac checkout inside the ARVO workspace container. The benchmark metadata names vulnerable commit `a6b64082b43226f51dff69a5e241049cf5e7eb83`, but the live line map used below is the staged checkout at `e95aaf2b8db33d4ac8b8c581ba5d34e839141798`, which still contains the pre-fix `gf_bs_set_eos_callback(bs, on_aom_av1_eos, state)` path removed by fix commit `9c74581c7827a6e1aea0f0a6f787ae22b4331a12`.

classification.classification_note: The saved crash is an AddressSanitizer stack-use-after-return WRITE. While parsing the first `av1C` box, `gf_av1_parse_obu` stores `on_aom_av1_eos` plus stack-local `AV1State state` in the shared `GF_BitStream`; the malformed OBU then leaves the `av1C` box short-read, `gf_isom_box_parse_ex` skips the unread 9-byte tail to the next root box, and the later size-zero `subs` box drives that same bitstream to EOF so `BS_ReadByte` dispatches the stale callback after `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size` has already returned.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42497316 (gpac): Stack-use-after-return WRITE 4 found by fuzz target fuzz_parse [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42497316
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is a 38-byte ISOBMFF fragment. Its first root box is `av1C` with size 22 and payload bytes `81 20 20 0d 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20`; its second root box is size 0 `subs`, so it extends to EOF and contributes full-box header bytes `20 20 20 20` plus trailing payload bytes `ff 20 20 20`. `av1c_box_read` passes the `av1C` payload into `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size`; inside `gf_av1_parse_obu`, GPAC installs `bs->EndOfStream = on_aom_av1_eos` and `bs->par = &state`, where `state` is the stack-local `AV1State` at `descriptors.c:1541`. The malformed first OBU then takes the `computed OBU size -1 (input value = 0)` path, so `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size` returns after only 5 of 14 `av1C` payload bytes were consumed, leaving that callback armed on the shared bitstream even though `state` has gone out of scope. Back in `gf_isom_box_parse_ex`, the short-read box is still accepted: `end-start < size`, so it computes `to_skip = 9` and calls `gf_bs_skip_bytes(bs, to_skip)`, advancing the same shared bitstream to the next root `subs` box. After the generic full-box header consumes `20 20 20 20`, `subs_box_read` materializes `entry_count = 0xff202020` from the last four bytes and enters the loop even though no payload bytes remain for the first entry. The next `gf_bs_read_u32` for `sample_delta` reaches EOF, `BS_ReadByte` dispatches the stale `on_aom_av1_eos(bs->par)` callback, and `on_aom_av1_eos` writes `state->bs_overread = GF_TRUE` through the dead stack pointer, producing the recorded AddressSanitizer stack-use-after-return WRITE of size 4.

source.description: First project parser statement on the vulnerable path that consumes attacker-controlled bytes on the shared `GF_BitStream`. It starts AV1 configuration parsing for the witness's first root box, which is where the stale end-of-stream callback state is created.
source.value_from: The exact staged witness is `gt_results/arvo_42497316/poc` (sha256 `51ded79197014d1f4e864acf49cc51dff958700e6e3540e19e74844ebb550a82`). Its prefix is `00 00 00 16 61 76 31 43 81 20 20 0d 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20`, so the first root box is `av1C` with declared payload size 14. This statement passes that payload into `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size` on the same bitstream object later reused by `subs_box_read`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The AV1 parser stores `on_aom_av1_eos` and the caller's `state` pointer in the shared bitstream even though `state` is the stack-local `AV1State` of `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size`. No later code clears that callback before the caller returns, so subsequent EOF on the same `GF_BitStream` writes through a dangling stack pointer.
root_cause.note: Fix commit `9c74581c7827a6e1aea0f0a6f787ae22b4331a12` removes `on_aom_av1_eos`, removes `AV1State.bs_overread`, and replaces this callback-based overread tracking with `gf_bs_mark_overflow()` / `gf_bs_is_overflow()` stored in the bitstream itself.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. EOF during `subs_box_read` dispatches the stale AV1 end-of-stream callback, and `on_aom_av1_eos` writes through a pointer to a returned stack `AV1State` object.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `stack-use-after-return` with `WRITE of size 4` here, and its frame-object dump says the bad address lies inside local variable `state` in `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size` at `src/odf/descriptors.c:1541`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the witness's trailing `subs` bytes first become the loop bound that reaches the sink. Because the size-zero `subs` box has only four payload bytes after its full-box header, those bytes are interpreted as `entry_count = 0xff202020`, which forces the first loop iteration even though no bytes remain for `sample_delta`.

parser_admitted.description: The saved ASan stack reaches `subs_box_read -> gf_bs_read_u32`, confirming that parsing continued on the same shared bitstream into the second root box before the stale callback fired.

av1_boundary_recovery.description: The saved run logs `[ISOBMFF] AV1ConfigurationBox: read only 5 bytes (expected 14)` and then `[iso file] Box "av1C" (start 0) has 9 extra bytes`, matching this branch: `end-start < size` computes `to_skip = 9` and `gf_bs_skip_bytes(bs, to_skip)` skips the unread tail of the short-read `av1C` box so parsing resumes at the next root box on the same `GF_BitStream`.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 stayed source-grounded and did not add instrumentation.

Stage 01 reproduced only the vulnerable image. `prepare_report.json` says `fix_image_available` is false, so Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image; `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` therefore remains false even though `patch.diff` directly removes the stale callback mechanism used here.

The benchmark metadata's `vulnerable_commit` does not match the live staged source tree used for line mapping. Every line below is anchored to the prepared checkout that Stage 01 actually compiled and ran (`e95aaf2b8db33d4ac8b8c581ba5d34e839141798`).

coarse_trace.summary: The first `av1C` root box is parsed on the shared bitstream and entered into the AV1 configuration reader.

The AV1 parser installs `on_aom_av1_eos` with stack-local `AV1State state` as callback parameter, then the malformed OBU takes the `computed OBU size -1` path and the caller returns after consuming only part of the `av1C` payload while that callback remains armed.
The generic box parser accepts the short-read `av1C` box, computes `to_skip = 9`, and skips the unread tail so the same bitstream advances to the next root `subs` box.
The next size-zero `subs` box turns its final four bytes into a huge `entry_count` and immediately tries to read the first `sample_delta` at EOF.
EOF dispatches the stale callback stored on the shared bitstream, and the callback writes through returned stack `state`, triggering the recorded stack-use-after-return.

fine_trace.note: Source. The exact witness starts with a size-22 `av1C` root box, so `av1c_box_read` passes its 14-byte payload into `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size` on the shared `GF_BitStream`.

While parsing that AV1 payload, `gf_av1_parse_obu` stores `on_aom_av1_eos` and pointer `state` in the shared bitstream. Here `state` is the stack-local `AV1State` in `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size` at `descriptors.c:1541`, so the bitstream now owns a pointer into its caller's stack frame.

The malformed first OBU reaches the `computed OBU size -1 (input value = 0)` branch because the header has no size field and the incoming `*obu_size` is 0. `gf_av1_parse_obu` therefore exits in error immediately after step 2 installed the callback.

After the logged parse failure at position 12, `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size` breaks out of the OBU loop, calls `gf_av1_reset_state(&state, GF_TRUE)`, and returns after only 5 of the 14 `av1C` payload bytes were consumed. That ends the stack frame that owns `state`, but no code has cleared `bs->EndOfStream` or `bs->par`, so the shared bitstream still holds a dangling pointer to returned stack storage and remains 9 bytes short of the `av1C` box boundary.

The generic box parser recovers from that short read instead of aborting. With `size = 22` for the root `av1C` box and `end-start = 13` after only 5 payload bytes were consumed, this branch computes `to_skip = 9` and skips the unread tail of the same box. The shared `GF_BitStream` is therefore advanced to the next root box header (`subs`) while step 2's stale callback remains installed.

After step 5 skips the unread `av1C` tail, parsing reaches the next root box on the same bitstream. That second box is size-zero `subs`, so after its full-box header there are only four payload bytes left; this statement materializes those bytes as `entry_count = 0xff202020`, which is nonzero and leaves no bytes remaining for the first sub-sample entry.
Because step 6 made `entry_count` nonzero, the loop enters its first iteration and tries to read `sample_delta`. At this point the bitstream is already at EOF, so this read has no bytes available.

At the EOF reached in step 7, the shared bitstream takes its read-mode end-of-stream path and calls the callback fields that step 2 left installed. No `subs` code clears or replaces `bs->EndOfStream` or `bs->par` before this point.

Sink. Step 8 dispatches `on_aom_av1_eos` with `bs->par` still pointing at step 2's `AV1State state` from `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size`. That function has already returned in step 4, so this 4-byte store lands in stack-after-return memory. ASan reports `WRITE of size 4` here and names `state` (`descriptors.c:1541`) as the poisoned stack object.

patch_analysis.patch_description: Fix commit `9c74581c7827a6e1aea0f0a6f787ae22b4331a12` introduces bitstream-local overflow tracking (`gf_bs_mark_overflow`, `gf_bs_is_overflow`), removes `AV1State.bs_overread` and `on_aom_av1_eos`, and updates AV1/VP9/AVC/HEVC/VVC readers to consult the bitstream overflow state instead of storing parser-local stack addresses in `GF_BitStream` callbacks.

key_changes.change: Replaces `gf_bs_set_eos_callback(bs, on_aom_av1_eos, state)` with `gf_bs_mark_overflow(bs, GF_TRUE)` and overflow checks, so the shared bitstream no longer stores a pointer to stack-local `AV1State`.
Removes the `bs_overread` field from `AV1State`, eliminating the stale stack field written by `on_aom_av1_eos`.
Adds explicit overflow state APIs so short-read detection lives in the bitstream object itself rather than in per-call parser stack variables.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image. The staged patch still provides source evidence because it removes `on_aom_av1_eos`, removes `AV1State.bs_overread`, and replaces the callback registration in `gf_av1_parse_obu` with bitstream-local overflow tracking.
sanitizer_ground_truth.evidence_note: The saved `sanitizer_trace.txt` reports `stack-use-after-return` at `src/media_tools/av_parsers.c:4095` and explicitly says the bad address lies inside object `state` in frame `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size` at `src/odf/descriptors.c:1539`; the frame-object dump identifies the poisoned local as `state` declared at line 1541.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42497316 run --version vulnerable --expect crash` and reproduced the AddressSanitizer stack-use-after-return in `on_aom_av1_eos`.

format.name: Exact 38-byte ISOBMFF av1C+subs fragment
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 38-byte witness `gt_results/arvo_42497316/poc` (sha256 `51ded79197014d1f4e864acf49cc51dff958700e6e3540e19e74844ebb550a82`). That file must keep the same observed two-box layout: first a size-22 `av1C` root box whose payload is exactly `81 20 20 0d 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20`, then a size-zero `subs` root box whose full-box header is `20 20 20 20` and whose only remaining payload bytes are `ff 20 20 20`. On that witness, the AV1 parser must still install `on_aom_av1_eos` with stack-local `AV1State state` in the shared `GF_BitStream`, the malformed `av1C` OBU must still take the logged `computed OBU size -1 (input value = 0)` path, `gf_isom_box_parse_ex` must still compute `to_skip = 9` and skip the unread tail of `av1C` so parsing reaches the next root `subs` box on the same bitstream, and `subs_box_read` must still parse `entry_count = 0xff202020` and then request `sample_delta` at EOF so `BS_ReadByte` dispatches the stale callback. This contract is limited to that exact staged witness and observed parse path; it does not generalize to other ISOBMFF files, AV1 configuration payloads, or `subs` boxes.
